_about: Weeks whose full (rank, song) ordering repeats the previous week, triaged and accepted. verify_charts.py reports these as warnings; anything not listed here fails the run. Keys starting with _ are ignored.
_top100: Every one is a New Year week, when Billboard historically republished the prior week's chart rather than compiling a new one. The sibling AC, country and alternative charts show 14-day publication gaps at the same dates, which is the same holiday behaviour recorded a different way. Genuine, not corrupt.
_albums200: Same New Year republication as top100.
_radio: New Year weeks, first two years of the chart's life, and the same dates top100 and albums200 already carry. Re-dated from 1990-12-26/1991-12-25 when the Wednesday-dated weeks were shifted to Billboard's real Saturday dates. Both were re-checked at source: Billboard serves each with its own 'Week of' heading and a full ~1.98 MB page, so the repeated ranking is a genuine frozen holiday chart, not a clamp.
_mainstream_rock: All thirteen were fetched individually on 2026-08-12 and every one serves its OWN 'Week of' heading at a full ~1.7 MB page with all 40 rows — the frozen-week signature, not the clamp signature (a clamp answers with a DIFFERENT heading, as 1984-12-29 does). So Billboard published these weeks and republished the prior ranking in them. Ten are New Year weeks and nine of those dates top100 already carries. 1983-07-02 is the Independence Day week; 1984-03-24 is the one freeze with no holiday behind it, but its evidence is identical to the rest. 1982-12-25 / 1983-01-01 / 1983-01-08 are a THREE-week freeze, which is why 1983-01-08 appears here too: the backfill's guard skipped 1983-01-01, leaving 1983-01-08 without the predecessor it would have been compared against, so it was stored. Filling 1983-01-01 makes both visible to the post-hoc check. Note 1984-12-29 is deliberately ABSENT from the CSV and from this list — Billboard serves 1985-01-05 for it, so Mainstream Rock never had that week, and the 14-day step there is correct.
_latin_pop_airplay: Two three-week freezes, each fetched individually on 2026-08-12 and each serving its OWN 'Week of' heading at full page size, which is the frozen-week signature rather than a clamp. 1994-10-15/22/29 all hold 'El Dia Que Me Quieras' on a chart that was ONE row deep at the time — at that depth an identical ranking is simply a song holding #1 and is not evidence of anything, so the heading is the only discriminator. 2004-09-25/10-02/10-09 is the same freeze Hot Latin Songs shows at those dates. The middle week of each freeze was skipped by the backfill's clamp guard, which removed the predecessor the third week would have been compared against and let the third through unnoticed; both middle weeks were filled afterwards so the pair is visible to this check.
_latin_airplay: The 2004 Latin freeze again — Billboard held one ranking across 09-25, 10-02 and 10-09, and all three serve their OWN 'Week of' heading at ~1.9 MB with 50 rows, so they were published rather than clamped. Hot Latin Songs and Latin Pop Airplay show the same three weeks, which is what makes this a Billboard-wide freeze and not a per-chart artifact. 10-02 was skipped by the backfill's clamp guard and filled afterwards, so 10-09 has the predecessor it needs to be checked against.
_dance_club: Thirty-four weeks that repeat the ranking before them. All thirty-four were fetched individually on 2026-08-13 and every one serves its OWN 'Week of' heading at full page size with a full row count, which is the frozen-week signature: Billboard published the week and republished the prior ranking in it. Thirty-two are New Year weeks — the same republication top100 and albums200 carry, and nine of these dates top100 already lists. The other two are a September 1977 freeze (09-10 and 09-17 both repeat 09-03) with no holiday behind it, evidence identical to the rest. 1977-09-17 and 1994-01-01 were invisible until their predecessors were filled: the backfill had no week to compare them against, so it stored them unchecked — the predecessor-absent hole. The chart ended 2020-03-28 and the run has no missing week at all, so this list is final.
_tropical_airplay: Two freezes, each week fetched individually on 2026-08-13 and each serving its OWN 'Week of' heading at full page size. 1994-10-15/22 hold 'Quien Eres Tu' on a chart that was ONE row deep then — at that depth an identical ranking is just a song holding #1 and proves nothing either way, so the heading is the only discriminator, exactly as on latin_pop_airplay. 2004-10-02/10-09 is the Billboard-wide 2004 Latin freeze that Hot Latin Songs, Latin Airplay and Latin Pop Airplay all show at the same dates. Both middle weeks (1994-10-15, 2004-10-02) were skipped by the backfill's clamp guard, which removed the predecessor the following week would have been compared against and let it through unnoticed; both were filled afterwards, which is what made 1994-10-22 and 2004-10-09 visible to this check at all.
_regional_mexican_airplay: Same 2026-08-13 pass, same heading test. 1994-10-15 holds 'La Nina Fresa' at ONE row deep, so the heading is again the only evidence. 1996-10-26 repeats the full 20-row ordering of 1996-10-19 under its own heading at ~1.31 MB. This chart does NOT carry the 2004 Latin freeze and its 1994-10-22 differs from 1994-10-15, so neither is listed — the guard is discriminating here, not waved through.
_christian_albums: Three holiday weeks that repeat the ranking before them. All three were fetched individually on 2026-08-16 and every one serves its OWN 'Week of' heading at full page size with its full row count (1983-12-17 and 1984-01-07 at 27 rows / ~1.40 MB, 1991-12-28 at 40 rows / ~1.65 MB) — the frozen-week signature, not the clamp signature. 1991-12-28 is a date top100, albums200, radio, mainstream_rock and dance_club already carry, which is what makes it a Billboard-wide New Year republication rather than a per-chart artifact. Note this chart published roughly monthly through the 1980s, so its 28-day steps are normal and the repeated ranking spans a month, not a week.
_gospel_albums: Same 2026-08-16 pass, same heading test: each of the five serves its own 'Week of' heading at full page size (1983-12-24 at 15 rows / ~1.18 MB, the other four at 25 rows / ~1.36 MB). Four are New Year weeks and 1988-12-31, 1990-12-29 and 1991-12-28 are dates top100 and albums200 already list. Like christian_albums this chart ran roughly monthly in the 1980s, so the 28-day steps are the chart's real cadence.
